A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same SUSD paper, with 21 complete pages including Appendices A-N. Text and rendered-page comparison establish identical research content, equations, figures and tables; only publication/version markings differ.

before.justification: v1 reports original SUSD experiments on downstream tasks, goal reaching, state coverage and factor decoding, plus appendix ablations and sensitivity analyses (Section 5, Tables 1-2 and Figures 3-13).

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including downstream returns, decoding errors, coverage measurements and appendix ablations.

M1.justification: The factorized embeddings, curiosity-based weighting, training objectives and Algorithm 1 are identical. The discrete-skill adaptation in Appendix F is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Ant, HalfCheetah, 2D-Gunner, Multi-Particle and Kitchen with the same downstream tasks and test scenarios, including those documented in the appendices.

E2.justification: LSD, CSD, METRA, DIAYN and DUSDi remain the evaluated baselines, with identical membership within corresponding comparisons. SkiLD remains discussed but unevaluated (Appendix D).

E3.justification: Evaluation procedures, metrics, model configurations and budgets are unchanged. Examples include the 20K-step goal-reaching evaluation, decoder data splits of 80%/10%/10%, and settings in Tables 3-4.

E4.justification: Both retain the same component ablations, discrete-versus-continuous comparison, factor-grouping analysis, baseline skill-dimensionality analysis, bin coverage and over/under-factorization tests (Appendices F-I, K and M).

E5.justification: Figure 3 retains means and standard deviations over three random seeds. Figure 6 retains eight seeds, and Table 2 retains eight independent runs and identical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and plotted results are identical. For example, Table 1 retains SUSD decoding errors of 0.060, 0.014 and 0.080 for Multi-Particle, Kitchen and 2D-Gunner, respectively.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives, Lemma 4.1 and its Appendix A proof are unchanged. Appendix F also retains the same discrete-skill reward formula.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain identical claims about factorized skill discovery, adaptive curiosity weighting and performance in structured environments.

C2.justification: Interpretations and applicability qualifications are identical, including the assumption of direct state-vector access and Appendix M's explanation of performance degradation under inappropriate factorization.

D1.justification: Implementation information in Appendices E and J, hyperparameters in Tables 3-4, and the public code link are unchanged. No reproducibility details are added or removed.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography and positioning relative to MI-based, DSD-based and factorized approaches are identical. The publication-status header does not revise research positioning.

P1.justification: The running header changes from 'Accepted' to 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026'. The arXiv stamp updates from v1 dated 2 February 2026 to v2 dated 3 June 2026. Body wording and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: All 13 figures and four tables retain identical content, captions, formatting and placement. Rendered body pages match exactly; the header and version-stamp wording updates do not reorganize the layout.

improvement.justification: v2 only updates publication-status and arXiv version/date markings. The research content, supporting evidence, explanations and presentation throughout the main text and appendices are unchanged, establishing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
